# Auto-generated Key Backfill

Dameng database's auto-increment columns are well-suited for backfilling via JDBC generated keys. Under the Dameng dialect, dbVisitor does not optimize INSERTs requiring primary key backfill into batch generated keys; instead, it conservatively executes row by row.

## Lambda / BaseMapper

```java title='Dameng auto-increment column mapping'
@Table("user_info")
public class UserInfo {
    @Column(value = "id", primary = true, keyType = KeyType.Auto)
    private Long id;

    @Column("name")
    private String name;
}
```

```java title='Read backfilled primary key after Lambda insert'
UserInfo user = new UserInfo();
user.setName("mali");

LambdaTemplate lambda = ...
lambda.insert(UserInfo.class)
      .applyEntity(user)
      .executeSumResult();

Long id = user.getId();
```

## Mapper XML

```xml title='Dameng generated keys'
<insert id="insertUser"
        useGeneratedKeys="true"
        keyProperty="id"
        keyColumn="id">
    INSERT INTO user_info (name)
    VALUES (#{name})
</insert>
```

Recommend explicitly writing `keyColumn` to keep the backfill column consistent with the business primary key column.

## Annotation Mapper

```java
@Insert(
    value = "INSERT INTO user_info (name) VALUES (#{name})",
    useGeneratedKeys = true,
    keyProperty = "id",
    keyColumn = "id"
)
int insertUser(UserInfo user);
```

## Sequence

Dameng supports sequences. The Dameng official FAQ describes using `schema.sequence.NEXTVAL` to get the next value and `schema.sequence.CURRVAL` to get the current value. dbVisitor's Dameng dialect generates:

```sql
SELECT user_info_seq.NEXTVAL
```

Mapper XML can use `selectKey`:

```xml
<insert id="insertUser">
    <selectKey keyProperty="id" keyColumn="id" order="BEFORE">
        SELECT user_info_seq.NEXTVAL AS id
    </selectKey>
    INSERT INTO user_info (id, name)
    VALUES (#{id}, #{name})
</insert>
```

Annotations:

```java
@SelectKeySql(
    value = "SELECT user_info_seq.NEXTVAL AS id",
    keyProperty = "id",
    keyColumn = "id",
    order = Order.Before
)
@Insert("INSERT INTO user_info (id, name) VALUES (#{id}, #{name})")
int insertUser(UserInfo user);
```

Lambda / BaseMapper can use `KeyType.Sequence`:

```java
@KeySeq("user_info_seq")
@Column(value = "id", primary = true, keyType = KeyType.Sequence)
private Long id;
```

## Conflict Strategies

The Dameng dialect's `Ignore` strategy uses the `IGNORE_ROW_ON_DUPKEY_INDEX` hint, requiring primary key columns. The `Update` strategy is implemented via `MERGE INTO`:

```sql
MERGE INTO user_info TMP
USING (SELECT ? id, ? name FROM dual) SRC
ON (TMP.id = SRC.id)
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET name = SRC.name
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, name) VALUES (SRC.id, SRC.name)
```

These syntaxes primarily affect insert conflict handling and do not change the generated keys reading model.

## Dialect Strategy

Dameng's current strategy is as follows:

| Scenario | GeneratedKeyStrategy |
| --- | --- |
| No backfill columns | `JdbcBatch` |
| `Into` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |
| `Ignore` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |
| `Update` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |

`DuplicateKeyStrategy.Ignore` requires primary key columns; `DuplicateKeyStrategy.Update` requires primary key columns and at least one non-primary key column that is updatable.

## Design Principles

- Auto-increment columns: use `KeyType.Auto` or `useGeneratedKeys=true`.
- sequence: use `selectKey` / `@SelectKeySql` / `KeyType.Sequence` to get value before INSERT.
- Conservative row-by-row execution when generated keys backfill is needed.
- General documentation: see [Generated Keys](../../guides/core/mapper/annotation_insert#generated-keys).
